land.text: the Itsekiri coast, settled by Prince Ginuwa, eldest son of Oba Olua of Benin

predecessors.note: The Benin Empire page lists the Itsekiri among Benin's subjects; the Warri page makes the kingdom sovereign, 'never under direct rule by another kingdom' (Bosman 1705: 'neighbour and ally').

land.text: Warri, under a protectorate treaty signed on 16 July 1884

successors.note: The page dates the end of Warri's autonomy to 1894 (the defeat of Nana Olomu); by 1900 Chief Dore Numa was paramount chief under the Southern Nigeria Protectorate.

capitals.name: Ijala (Ode-Itsekiri)
capitals.note: Placed at the gazetteer's Warri point; the page gives no coordinates. 'Earlier, the seat was at Ijala'; 'Olu Ijijen later moved the capital from Ijala to Ode-Itsekiri' (undated); the ancestral capital is Ode-Itsekiri in Warri South LGA.

correction.text: the Itsekiri kingdom of Warri on the Benin River: 'The sovereign of this state owns not only both banks of the Benin river' (Landolphe, undated)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The infobox gives no area; the only territorial description is Landolphe's account of the Benin River banks; a 30 km circle round Warri (about 2,800 km2) stands for it.

ledger.note: c. 1480: Prince Ginuwa founds the Warri kingdom. The kingdom 'was established in 1480' and 'founded around c. 1480 by Prince Ginuwa, the eldest son of Oba Olua of the Kingdom of Benin'; the migration 'began around 1470 with seventy Benin chiefs', which the page does not reconcile with Olua's accession in 1473.
1884 (16 July): the Warri chiefs sign a British protectorate treaty. 'Warri chiefs signed a protectorate treaty with British officials on 16 July 1884, with an addendum on 6 August.'
1884 (July): the sovereign kingdom ends; 'In 1894, after a dispute, the Royal Navy defeated Nana Olomu, ending Warri's autonomy'. The Olu's line continues to the present.

sources.title: Warri Kingdom
sources.note: Founded c. 1480 by Ginuwa of Benin; sovereign, Benin an ally (Bosman 1705, Dapper 1668); capitals Ijala and Ode-Itsekiri; protectorate treaty 16 July 1884; Nana Olomu 1894; Dore Numa by 1900; no area.

notes: The Warri Kingdom has no Cliopatria row. One page opened (the budget for a state with one keyframe is 1-2). The page contradicts itself on the founding (c. 1480, the migration c. 1470, Olua's reign from 1473) and gives no dates for Benin suzerainty, the capital move or the extent. It dates the end of autonomy to 1894 (the Royal Navy defeated Nana Olomu 'ending Warri's autonomy and integrating it into the Lagos Colony'; the war is in the Niger Coast Protectorate dossier); the dossier ends at the 16 July 1884 protectorate treaty so that it matches the Niger Coast Protectorate dossier, whose 1884 shape includes the Warri coast. A gap-filler may prefer 1894. The capital dot is the Warri gazetteer point, not Ode-Itsekiri.
